span.label: whether a penetrating electrode array in the inferior colliculus can restore useful hearing, and what stimulating different midbrain regions reveals about how the human auditory system is organised
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether stimulating along the tonotopic gradient of the human central nucleus produces ordered pitch percepts, as it does along the cochlea
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the implant is safe and gives loudness, temporal and directional percepts and speech benefit comparable with the brainstem implant, but the ordered pitch the whole rationale predicted did not appear
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Sustained stimulation rates and patterns overdrive adaptation-prone neurons in the dorsal IC, raising the current needed over time
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Neurons higher in the auditory pathway lose the ability to phase-lock, and that loss of temporal synchronization is traded for a spatial, spike-rate-based code of temporal features, which is why the midbrain follows lower rates than the fibre pathway below it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Ipsilaterally and contralaterally driven brainstem projections stay segregated as they ascend into the IC, so which region the array sits in determines the perceived direction of the sound
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The ipsilaterally excited fibre population is dominated by low-frequency-tuned neurons, so stimulating it yields low-pitch percepts
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: An array lying outside the IC acts as a surface electrode, so current must travel further to reach neurons and activation levels rise
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the central nucleus is chosen because it receives almost all ascending brainstem pathways, so it should give access to a more complete set of inputs than the cochlea or cochlear nucleus
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the limited performance of tumour patients with the brainstem implant is attributed to tumour damage in the cochlear nucleus, which is the argument for moving upstream
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: segregated monaural and binaural pathways ascending into the midbrain are proposed to explain why each patient perceived only one direction

span.label: ipsilaterally driven pathways carry mostly low frequencies, which is offered as the reason one patient heard only low pitches

span.label: temporal synchrony degrades at successive stages of the pathway, so a site below the colliculus should follow faster rates - which is what happened

span.label: long shallow loudness tails are read as a non-homogeneous mix of excitatory and inhibitory neurons along the isofrequency dimension

span.label: rising activation levels in one patient are hypothesised to be neurons in the dorsal region being overdriven by the stimulation pattern

'AMI sites are in direct contact with surrounding neurons, UNLIKE CI SITES; thus, THRESHOLDS SHOULD BE LOWER as shown in animal studies. However, AMI thresholds ... are 6-12 nC ..., and dynamic ranges are 7-9 dB, WHICH ARE SIMILAR TO THOSE OF THE CI.' The animal-derived expectation is not refuted in animals; it fails to transfer to the human implant. Q-448.

The poor outcomes of the original population are reattributed to the tumour rather than to the implant site - so a device evaluated only in tumour patients was being judged on a confound. Q-512.

The span: 'auditory nerve fibers CAN SYNCHRONIZE to high-rate (exceeding 1 kHz) ... stimulation, WHEREAS Quotation withheld.' The contrast is between AUDITORY NERVE FIBERS and NEURONS HIGHER ALONG THE PATHWAY; temporal resolution is the PROPERTY it turns on, named in the next clause as 'this degradation in tem[poral resolution]'. The edge keeps one side and the property. Same shape as Halgren2006[19], retracted an hour ago. Found by the neighbour query (Q-400). Q-418. — strength of the relation: 1 — nerve fibres synchronise above a kilohertz while neurons higher up cannot, which is the standard account the lemniscal patient's threefold advantage fits

span.label: RETRACTED (AN EVIDENTIAL RELATION TAGGED AS A CAUSAL ONE) · animal models —causes→ tonotopic
span.note: RETRACTED: AN EVIDENTIAL RELATION TAGGED AS A CAUSAL ONE. The edge is `animal models --causes--> tonotopic`. Animal models are WHERE the tonotopic organisation was demonstrated, not what produces it: 'the well defined tonotopic organization of its central nucleus. THIS HAS BEEN SHOWN EXTENSIVELY IN ANIMAL MODELS ... and, BECAUSE of the similarities in the anatomical structure of the IC across mammalian species, it was INFERRED that such a functional organization exists within the human ICC.' The `because` governs an inference about cross-species similarity licensing a transfer to humans - it says nothing about what causes tonotopy. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): that a finding in animals was EXTENDED to humans by an anatomical-similarity argument. That is a claim about the warrant for a transfer, which `transfers` records and `concept_edges` cannot, so nothing is kept here. — strength of the relation: 1 — the human organisation was INFERRED from anatomical similarity across mammals before anyone could test it
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Three NF2 patients were implanted with a penetrating auditory midbrain implant and the device proved safe, with the array showing minimal movement over time.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Midbrain stimulation delivered usable loudness, pitch, temporal and directional percepts.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: All three patients gained lip-reading enhancement and environmental sound awareness, with speech perception on a par with NF2 auditory brainstem implant patients.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Contrary to the animal-derived prediction, stimulating successive depths along the ICC tonotopic gradient did not produce an ordered pitch shift, and every site in every patient sounded predominantly low-pitched.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Pulse trains fused into a continuous percept above about 50-80 pps when stimulating the inferior colliculus, i.e. roughly 20 ms temporal resolution, far coarser than the 250-300 pps of cochlear stimulation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The patient implanted at the lateral lemniscus rather than in the IC still heard buzzing up to 220 pps, about three times the rate the IC-implanted patients could follow.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Perceived sound direction was fixed within each patient but differed by implant location: ipsilateral for the lateral-lemniscus placement and contralateral for the dorsomedial ICC placement.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Despite electrodes sitting directly among midbrain neurons, thresholds (6-12 nC) and dynamic ranges (7-9 dB) were no better than those of a cochlear implant.

span.label: Loudness grew monotonically with current level in all three patients, so level cues can be coded systematically from the midbrain.
